mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE > 6%) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when UNRATE exceeds 6%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) with high unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a lagging labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive with strong PAYEMS and high UNRATE, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, high FEDFUNDS predicts negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in a tightening cycle, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher with rising RSAFS, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 110) signals supply weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO is below 110, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) with high FEDFUNDS indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive with GDPC1 growth and high FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment (UNRATE) may not prevent market decline, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in late-cycle with low UNRATE, or Rank IC < 0.03.
